welcome.title: Welcome to Pattern Projector!
welcome.description: Pattern projector is a free and open source web app that quickly calibrates projectors for sewing patterns. It also has tools for stitching together multiple page patterns, changing line thickness, inverting colors, flipping/rotating patterns, and more. To read about the latest updates, check out the <changeLogLink>changelog</changeLogLink>.

requirements.title: What You’ll Need
requirements.mat: A cutting mat with grid lines (optional)
requirements.mount: Tripod or wall/shelf/table mount for projector
requirements.computer: Computer or tablet to connect to the projector

setup.title: Setup
setup.place: Place the projector above the cutting mat, pointing directly at the cutting mat. If you do not have a cutting mat, you can use paper or masking tape to mark out a grid/rectangle on a table or floor.
setup.connect: Connect your computer or tablet to the projector and either mirror or extend the display so that image from computer or tablet is shown on the projector.
setup.focus: Adjust the focus on the projector, until text is crisp in the centre of the projection. If you cannot get a clear image, ensure the distance between the projector and cutting mat is within the functional range recommended by the manufacturer.
setup.keystone: If your projector has a keystone, adjust it so that projection is close to rectangular and focus near the edges improves.

calibration.title: Calibration
calibration.start: Click (or tap) “Start Calibrating.” This opens your patterns. Click (or tap) “Calibrate” there, or open a pattern and you will calibrate first if needed.
calibration.fullscreen: Calibration happens in full screen, so the measurements match when you cut. If the app is not in full screen yet, click (or tap) <fullscreenIcon></fullscreenIcon> at the top of the screen.
calibration.guide: New users get a step-by-step guide with a small printable target. You can open it any time with “Guided setup.”
calibration.drag: Drag the corners of the grid to align with your mat. With your eyes on the mat, adjust the corners on your computer or tablet. Adjust the placement of the corners until the projected grid matches your mat's grid.
calibration.size: You don't have to calibrate using your entire mat, instead choose the largest area you can fit the calibration grid in and input the width and height to match the width and height of the grid.
calibration.lens: If straight lines bow near the edges of the projection, raise “Lens” a little at a time until they look straight. The corners stay where they are.
calibration.project: When the projected grid is aligned with your mat, click (or tap) “Save calibration.” “Cancel” puts the previous calibration back.

project.title: Projecting a Pattern
project.open: Add a PDF or SVG pattern on the patterns screen, then click (or tap) it to open it in full screen. Patterns are saved in this browser, so next time you only need to click the one you want.
project.switch: To switch patterns without leaving full screen, click (or tap) “Projects.” Each pattern reopens where you left it.
project.move: Move the PDF by clicking and dragging it around the screen.
project.tools: In projection mode there are several tools provided. Some have keyboard shortcuts, which are denoted in parentheses.

fullscreen.title: Full screen
fullscreen.description: It's generally easier to use the software in full screen mode.

showMenu.title: Show/hide menu
showMenu.description: Show or hide the top menu.

invert.title: Invert Colors
invert.description: When projecting, it's usually easier to see green or white lines on black. Click/tap once for green lines, twice for white lines, and three times to return to black lines.

moveTool.title: Show or hide move tool
moveTool.description: The move tool has four arrow buttons to move the calibration grid corners/edges. It also has a next button in the middle for switching to the next corner/edge.

overlayOptions.title: Show or hide overlay options
overlayOptions.description: Grid, border, paper sheet, flip lines, or wrong side overlays can be shown on the PDF to help with calibration and cutting. For more information, see the <overlayOptionsLink>overlay options section</overlayOptionsLink>.

lineWeight.title: Line weight
lineWeight.description: Change the thickness of the lines in the PDF pattern.

flip.title: Flip Vertical (V) or Horizontal (H)
flip.description: Helpful when mirroring patterns in half.

rotate.title: Rotate (R)
rotate.description: Change the orientation of the pattern by 90 degrees.

recenter.title: Center and Reset (C)
recenter.description: Centers the pattern on the cutting mat and resets the rotation/flipping.

magnify.title: Magnify (M)
magnify.description: Click (or tap) on the PDF to magnify it. Click (or tap) again to stop magnifying.

zoomOut.title: Zoom out (Z)
zoomOut.description: Zoom out to see the whole PDF. Click (or tap) on the PDF to zoom back in at selected location.

layers.title: Show or hide layers
layers.description: Show or hide layers in the PDF.

stitch.title: Show or hide stitch menu
stitch.description: Show or hide the stitch menu, which allows you to stitch together multiple page PDF patterns.

scale.title: Show or hide the scale menu
scale.description: Change size of the pattern by entering a multiplier: between 0-1 will make the pattern smaller and greater than 1 will make the pattern larger.

measure.title: Line tool (L)
measure.description: Mark lines on the PDF for rotating, flipping, moving, measuring, or marking. For a detailed description of the line tool, see the <lineToolLink>line tool section</lineToolLink>.

lineTool.title: Line Tool
lineTool.description: The line tool can be used to measure distances, mark lines on, rotate, flip, and move the PDF. Click (or tap) the line tool button, then click (or tap) on the PDF and drag to draw a line. Once a line is drawn, a menu will appear on the bottom of the screen with the following options:

rotate.title: Align to center
rotate.description: Rotates the PDF so the selected line is horizontal and centered on your mat.
rotate.use: For aligning the grain of a pattern piece with the grain of your fabric: draw a line on the grain line of the pattern piece, then click (or tap) the align to center button.

previousNext.title: Bring previous/next line to center
previousNext.description: Moves the PDF so that the previous/next line drawn is horizontal and centered on your mat.
previousNext.use: For moving between pattern pieces when cutting: draw a line on the grain line of each pattern piece, then move through the pattern pieces using these buttons. Delete lines as you move through the pattern pieces to keep track of which pieces are left to be cut.

flip.title: Flip along line
flip.description: Flips the PDF along the line.
flip.use: For unfolding pattern pieces: draw a line on the fold line of a pattern piece, cut the piece up to the fold line, click (or tap) the flip along line button, and then cut the remainder of the piece.

move.title: Move PDF by line length
move.description: Moves the PDF by the length of the line.
move.use: For lengthening/shortening pattern pieces: draw a line perpendicular the lengthen/shorten line of a pattern piece, cut to the lengthen/shorten line, then click (or tap) the move by line length button, and then continue cutting the piece. The direction of the line drawn will depend on whether you are lengthening or shortening the pattern piece.

length.title: Line length
length.description: Displays the length of the selected line (shown in purple). Other lines are orange.
length.use: Tap the length to enter a precise measurement and adjust the line's size. Useful for lengthening/shortening pattern pieces. See <lineToolVideoLink>this video</lineToolVideoLink> for an example.

angle.title: Line angle
angle.description: Displays the angle of the selected line (shown in purple). Other lines are orange.
angle.use: Enter a precise angle to rotate the line and pattern piece. Use the <alignIcon></alignIcon> align to center button to apply the rotation based on the entered angle.

overlayOptions.title: Overlay Options
overlayOptions.description: The overlay options can be used to verify calibration while projecting and help with cutting patterns. The following options are available:

border.title: Border
border.description: Shows the border of the calibration grid.

paper.title: Paper Sheet
paper.description: Shows a rectangle the size of a Letter or A4 piece of paper to verify calibration.

flipLines.title: Flip Lines
flipLines.description: Shows lines that help with unfolding patterns. Line the fold line of the pattern up with the flip line and press flip horizontally or vertically to mirror the piece.

flippedPattern.title: Wrong side
flippedPattern.description: Shows dots when the wrong side of the pattern is projected.

wrongSizePdf.question: Is your PDF projecting too small or large?
wrongSizePdf.answer: The Pattern Projector calibration tool has no zoom because the scale of the projection comes from the size information in the PDF. Patterns from designers usually have the correct scale, so a change in scale could have been introduced when opening the pattern in Affinity Designer or Inkscape.

saveAsApp.answer: Pattern Projector is a Progressive Web App (PWA) so it can be saved as an app. On a Desktop, you can install it using <googleChromeLink>Chrome</googleChromeLink> or <microsoftEdgeLink>Edge</microsoftEdgeLink>. On a tablet, open the Share menu and tap Add to Home Screen.

mobileSupport.question: Do you have support mobile phones and tablets?
mobileSupport.answer: While possible to visit and use the webpage on a smart phone, the limited screen size makes it difficult to use.

InstallButton.title: Install App
InstallButton.description: For the best experience, install Pattern Projector using <chromeLink>Google Chrome</chromeLink>. In Chrome, download the app by tapping <installIcon></installIcon> in the address bar.
InstallButton.descriptionAndroid: For the best experience on Android, use Firefox. Download the app by tapping the more button <moreIcon></moreIcon> in the browser menu and then <addToHomeScreenIcon></addToHomeScreenIcon> Add to Home Screen.
InstallButton.descriptionIOS: Download the app by tapping the share button <shareIcon></shareIcon> in the browser menu and then Add to Home Screen <addBoxIcon></addBoxIcon>.

Troubleshooting.title: Calibration Troubleshooting

dragCorners.title: How to calibrate
dragCorners.description: Drag the corners of the grid to at least a 24x16 inch rectangle on your mat. The grid should be as large as possible but does not need to cover the entire mat.
dragCorners.caption: A correctly calibrated grid.

Troubleshooting.inputMeasurement: Use a measuring tape to measure the width and height of the grid on your mat. Input these measurements into the width and height fields.

offByOne.title: Lines are straight but don’t align?
offByOne.description: If the projected lines are straight but don’t align with your mat, your width or height might be off by 1 inch/centimeter. Double-check your measurements with a measuring tape. Mat measurements can be confusing or inaccurate, so checking with a measuring tape is important.
offByOne.caption: The wrong measurements are input (23 x 17) instead of (24 x 18). The mat only shows numbers up to 23 and 17 so it is easy to confuse the measurements. Make sure you measure with a measuring tape!

unevenSurface.title: Curved lines?
unevenSurface.description: If the projected lines look curved, your mat or surface below the mat may not be flat. Try to flatten the mat but putting card stock under the low points or move to a different cutting surface.
unevenSurface.caption: This mat has a ruler under it causing the lines to curve in the center. A slight curve is ok but a large curve will cause issues.

dimensionsSwapped.title: Rectangles instead of squares?
dimensionsSwapped.description: If the projected grid looks like rectangles instead of squares, the width and height may be swapped. Simply swap the values in the fields.
dimensionsSwapped.caption: The width and height are in the wrong boxes. The dimension should read 'W: 24' and 'H: 18'.

Header.lensCorrectionDescription: Lens correction: if straight lines in the calibration grid bow outwards or inwards near the edges, adjust this until they look straight, then recalibrate the corners
Header.calibrationAlertContinue: The window size can't change after calibration. To project in full screen, calibrate in full screen. If you want to change the window size, recalibrate.
Header.stitchMenuDisabled: Open PDF to use stitch menu
Header.invalidCalibration: The calibration grid is not valid. Press 'Reset calibration' to try again.
Header.projectOpenError: That project's pattern file couldn't be loaded from this browser. Try opening the file again.
Header.invalidFile: {name} isn't a PDF or SVG pattern, so it can't be added.
Header.patternAdded: {name} is added. Click it to start projecting.
Header.projectSaveError: This browser couldn't save the pattern.
Header.calibrateInFullScreen: Calibrate in full screen so measurements stay correct while you cut.

calibrationMismatch.uncalibrated: This screen hasn't been calibrated yet. Calibrate so measurements are correct.
calibrationMismatch.calibratedInFullScreen: You calibrated in full screen, so go back to full screen to keep measurements correct.
calibrationMismatch.calibratedInWindow: You calibrated in a window, but you're projecting in full screen. Recalibrate in full screen so measurements are correct.
calibrationMismatch.sizeChanged: The screen size has changed since you calibrated (it was {was}, now it's {now}). Plugging in or unplugging a projector can do this, for example when the screen mirrors the projector. Recalibrate so measurements are correct.
calibrationMismatch.windowMoved: The window has moved since you calibrated. Recalibrate so measurements are correct.

Header.calibrationReminder: Calibration doesn't match this screen. Recalibrate before cutting.

SaveMenu.saveTooltip: Export PDF with stitched pages and selected layers
SaveMenu.encryptedPDF: This PDF is encrypted. Please enter the password to save the stitched PDF.

PdfViewer.noData: Press the "Open" button to load a pattern

print.title: Print the target
print.description: Print the target at 100% (Actual size) and check that the box measures 8 × 6 inches. Set W and H above to the size of the grid you're calibrating to on your mat, then put the target in the middle of that grid with the arrow pointing to the top of the mat.

align.title: Line up the target
align.description: Drag to move the purple target until its cross sits on the printed cross. Then resize and rotate it until the purple box sits on the printed box.
align.hint: Each click is a small step; hold Shift for bigger steps. You can also scroll or pinch to resize, and hold Shift while scrolling to rotate.

lens.title: Straighten the lines
lens.description: Remove the paper. If the projected grid lines bow outwards or inwards between the corners, adjust the lens correction until they run straight along your mat's lines. The corners stay where you put them. Skip this if the lines already match.

corners.title: Fine-tune the corners
corners.description: Drag each corner circle onto the matching corner of the grid on your mat. Click a corner and use the arrow keys to nudge it.

Projects.title: Projects
Projects.empty: No patterns yet. Add a PDF or SVG pattern and it stays here, so you can switch between patterns without finding the file again.
Projects.name: Project name
Projects.addFromHome: To add a new pattern, go to all patterns. That leaves full screen so you can choose the file.

ProjectsHome.title: Your patterns
ProjectsHome.dropHint: Drop a PDF or SVG pattern here, or choose one from your computer.
ProjectsHome.note: Opening a pattern goes full screen. If you haven't calibrated in full screen yet, you'll calibrate first. Patterns are kept in this browser on this device.
